I'll start by reading the format doc and inspecting the data.

Now samples of each format.

That call was malformed. I'll survey directives, headers and encodings across all files with a script.

The heredoc never got written because the earlier call failed. I'll write it with `write_file` and rerun.

The checker reports every value matches. Next I'll check for silently skipped or unparsed records, since the script has to work on other exports too.

I wrote `/app/bin/summarize.py` and ran it on `/app/data`. It took about 1.4 s and wrote `/app/out/summary.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_summary.py` reports "OK: every value matches the reference figures for /app/data". I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

It handles each depot's base format plus the shared conventions from `exports.md`. The ones that appear in the current data are:
- gzip files, UTF-8/UTF-16 byte order marks and `# charset: windows-1252`;
- directives and header rows that change part way through a file, including east rows that carry their own weight unit;
- quoted notes spanning lines, including ones that contain lines starting with `#`;
- south layout switches by record length and the printed page headers.

Exports are applied per depot in ascending `seq`, using the sequence number written inside each file.

I read the layout and weight rules from the docs rather than from the data, so other exports should parse the same way. Only the current `/app/data` has been run, though. The checker can't tell me how it does on other exports.

On the current files, every record parsed with a date and a known status, and every correction or void followed a matching new record.

`summary-format.md` showed two different pairs of weight constants. My first read showed 1 lb = 0.45392 kg and 1 oz = 0.02837 kg. The file on disk, checked again with `grep`, says 0.45359237 and 0.028349523125. I used the on-disk values, and the checker's figures agree with them.

cd /app/docs; grep -n 'lb' -r . ; md5sum summary-format.md; sed -n 1,200p exports.md | head -60; cat layouts/*

cd /app/data; for f in river-w1.* south-w1.* west-w1.*; do echo "=== $f"; head -c 1300 $f | cat -A | cut -c1-200 | head -18; done; file * | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//' | sort | uniq -c

cd /app/data; grep -n -B3 -A2 'overflow' east-w*.csv | head -40; grep -n -A3 'columns changed' lakeside*.csv | cut -c1-150| head -30; grep -n 'batch\|charset' east-*.csv | head -20; grep -c . /dev/null; head -c 600 east-w10.csv | cat -A | head;

cd /app/data; sed -n 333,340p east-w10.csv; grep -n '^# unit\|^# dates\|^# weight\|^# date' east-*.csv lakeside-*.csv river-*.tsv west-*.csv | awk -F: '{c[$1]++; print}' | awk -F: '{n[$1]++; l[$1]=l[$1]" "$2":"$3":"$4} END{for(k in n) if(n[k]>2) print k,l[k]}'
cd /tmp/s; python3 s2.py > o2.txt 2>&1; echo $?; wc -l o2.txt; cut -c1-300 o2.txt

cd /tmp/s; cat >> s2.py <<'EOF'
print('----')
P=collections.Counter()
for fn in sorted(os.listdir(D)):
    if not fn.startswith('east'): continue
    b=open(os.path.join(D,fn),'rb').read()
    if b[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b': b=gzip.decompress(b)
    t=b.decode('latin-1')
    lines=t.split('\n'); i=0
    while i<len(lines):
        l=lines[i]; i+=1
        if not l.strip() or l.startswith('#'): continue
        while l.count('"')%2 and i<len(lines): l+='\n'+lines[i]; i+=1
        f=next(csv.reader([l]))
        if len(f)==8:
            P[(fn,tuple(j for j,x in enumerate(f) if x in('kg','lb','oz','g')))]+=1
for k,v in sorted(P.items()): print(v,k)
EOF
python3 s2.py | sed -n '/----/,$p'
cd /app/data; grep -n '^#\|^id' east-w13.csv east-w3.csv east-w5.csv | cut -c1-120; sed -n '1,12p' east-w3.csv | cut -c1-120
cd /tmp/s; ls -la; python3 s3.py | cut -c1-200

cd /tmp/s; sed -i "s/else: t=b.decode('latin-1')/elif b[:3]==b'\\\\xef\\\\xbb\\\\xbf': t=b.decode('utf-8-sig')\n    else: t=b.decode('latin-1')/" s3.py; grep -n 'utf-8-sig' s3.py; python3 s3.py | cut -c1-200
cd /tmp/s; python3 s4.py | grep -v "'layout'" ; python3 s4.py | grep "'layout'" | head -30
cd /tmp/s; python3 s4.py | grep -v "'layout'" ; python3 s4.py | grep "'layout'" | head -30
cd /app && time python3 bin/summarize.py data out/summary.json; echo rc=$?; cat out/summary.json | head -50; python3 tools/check_summary.py
cd /tmp/s && python3 diag.py

cd /app && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/summarize.py, which parses all eight depot formats and the shared export conventions (gzip, BOM/charset, mid-file directives and headers, per-row units, layout switching) and applies the corrections, resend and handover rules. It ran on /app/data in about 1.4 s, wrote /app/out/summary.json, and check_summary.py reports every value matches."}
EOF
python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('STATUS.json')))"; python3 tools/check_summary.py
